rows: This tornado formed four miles west of Boys Ranch at 1751 CST and tracked north northeast. The tornado crossed U.S. Highway 385 at the Oldham and Hartley county line before exiting Oldham county at 1759 CST five miles northwest of Boys Ranch. The tornado continued in Hartley coun…
Trained spotter estimated winds at sixty miles an hour.
The hail was reported on U.S. Highway 385 about five miles south of the Canadian River.
The large hail broke out windows on several homes on the north and west sides of Adrian. No injuries were reported.
The large hail broke out two windows of a home. The hail also shredded leaves off of trees and covered the ground at least an inch deep. No injuries were reported.
A porch swing covering was reported to be ripped up and all foliage on vegetation was stripped. No injuries were reported.
A trained spotter reported that the large hail was breaking the windows in his home. No injuries were reported.
A truck driver reported that the windshield of his rig was broken from the large hail and the damage occurred near mile marker thirty-five on Interstate 40. No injuries were reported.

A tornado touched down about one mile west of Vega around 1708 CST and tracked east northeast for about one mile where it lifted around 1711 CST about one half of a mile north northwest of Vega. The tornado remained over open country and no damage or injuries were reported.
A trained spotter estimated the thunderstorm wind gust near Wildorado Texas.
A trained spotter also reported tree limbs down in Boys Ranch...however the trained spotter could not estimate the size of the tree limb while he was driving. No injuries were reported.
A storm chaser estimated the thunderstorm wind gusts in Vega Texas in Oldham County. No damage or injuries were reported.
A storm chaser estimated the thunderstorm wind gusts about one mile east of Vega Texas in Oldham County. There were no reports of damage or injuries.
The hail was completely covering the ground.

An official National Weather Service Storm Survey revealed that a tornado occurred four miles northwest of Adrian Texas in Oldham county around 1937CST and was on the ground for three minutes. The tornado was rated an EF0 with winds estimated near fifty-six knots. The tornado mov…
The hail was reported along Interstate 40.
The hail was reported to be two to three inches deep and completely covering the ground.

The Texas Department of Public Safety estimated the thunderstorm wind gusts about four miles east of Adrian Texas in Oldham county. There was no damage and there were no reports of injuries or fatalities.
A trained spotter reported that the thunderstorm wind gusts blew a six inch tree limb down. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities.
The Oldham County Sheriff's Office relayed a public report of part of a roof on a house was blown off by the thunderstorm wind gusts. There were no injuries or fatalities.

A trained spotter reported that thunderstorm wind gusts had blown down a telephone pole and also a storage building was destroyed and windows were broken in a residential structure. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities.
A storm chaser reported that the hail accumulated into drifts of three to four inches deep.

A storm chaser reported that the hail accumulated into drifts of three to four inches deep. Also, two tractor trailer rigs had slid off into a ditch along Interstate 40. There were no reports of damage and there were no injuries or fatalities.
A trained storm spotter estimated the thunderstorm wind gusts in the town of Adrian Texas in Oldham county.
Thunderstorm wind gusts caused damage to the roof of a gas station and also overturned a tractor trailer. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities.
The KVII schoolnet mesonet two miles to the east-southeast of Wildorado recorded a thunderstorm winds gust of 59 mph.
A trained spotter in Boys Ranch reported 1 inch hail.

As the line of thunderstorms moved across Oldham County from west to east it caused hazardous cross winds on north-south running roads, three tractor trailers on US Highway 385 were overturned. No injuries or fatalities were reported with these vehicle accidents.

As a line of thunderstorms moved across Oldham and Deaf Smith County, tree limbs were blown down in Adrian (Oldham County). An estimation of 60 mph outflow winds from the thunderstorms was determined using radar.

Pea to nickel size hail was reported 3 miles south of Boys Ranch.
Baseball size hail was reported 7 miles south of Channing.
Golf ball size hail was reported 5 miles northeast of Wildorado.
Two inch diameter hail was reported 2 miles north of Vega.
Quarter size hail was reported in Adrian.
Tree limbs 4 to 5 inches in diameter were reported down in Adrian from thunderstorm winds.
Nickel size hail was reported in Adrian.
Storm chasers reported a brief tornado over rural northern Oldham County. The tornado lasted for about one minute. This tornado was observed from Highway 385 just south of Boys Ranch.
Half dollar size hail was reported 5 miles north-northeast of Adrian. Accumulation of hail was reported.
Dime size hail was reported one mile southwest of Vega.
Reporting quarter hail 3 miles east of Vega on I-40. Hail now shifting north of highway.
Time estimated by radar. Time corrected.

Estimated dime to quarter size hail falling at time of the report.
Mostly dime to nickel size with a few larger than quarters.
No damage observed. Track and times estimated based on three separate videos and pictures.
Late report of ping pong ball size hail on Highway 385 north of Vega.
Storm chaser viewed brief tornado looking northeast from Adrian. Time of tornado was estimated by radar and video feed.
Golf ball size hail reported west of Vega on I-40.
Hail up to the size of quarters (1) reported at Boys Ranch.
Late report of quarter size hailstones.
Lat report of half dollar hail. Time estimated by radar.
Brief touchdown on a cattle ranch in NW Oldham County launched a feeder the size of a pickup truck over 300 yards. Otherwise, the tornado remained in open country consisting of mainly grasslands.
Late report of Ping Pong ball hail on I-40.
Sheriff reported half dollar sized hail.
Late report of ping pong ball hail on I-40.
Late report of tornado touchdown, with power flashes noted by chaser on Tascosa Road looking back towards Vega wind farm.
A spotter network report was received for quarter sized hail approximately 10 miles south of Boys Ranch along US Highway 385. There were also a few hailstones larger than 1.00 inch in diameter.
Very large hail fell up to 3.25 inches in diameter 3 miles east-southeast of Vega.
This gust was measured at the West Texas Mesonet station 1 mile west-southwest of Boys Ranch.
Ten 65-foot power poles and two 40-foot power poles were snapped due to thunderstorm winds. The time of occurrence has been estimated from radar data.
Tennis ball size hail fell 2 miles east of Vega.
Half dollar size hail fell in Vega.
Golf ball size hail fell 4 miles east-southeast of Vega. The time of occurrence has been estimated from radar data.
Hen egg size hail fell 5 miles west of Wildorado.
A tractor trailer was flipped on Interstate-40 at mile marker 42.
Multiple tractor trailers were flipped at mile marker 35 on Interstate-40.
This gust was measured at the West Texas Mesonet station 11 miles south-southwest of Romero.
A 64 mph gust was measured at the West Texas Mesonet station 11 miles south-southwest of Romero. No damage was reported.

The tornado touched down in very rural portions of Oldham county|and remained in open prairie grassland with no structures or|trees hit and no damage reported. The entire life cycle of the|tornado was documented by a local storm spotter.
Multiple gusts in excess of 58 mph were measured by a mesonet. Maximum wind gust of 69 mph occurred at 1928 CDT.
Thunderstorm collapsed right on top of the mesonet.
From the station located near Vega, TX.
Quarter to golfball size hail fell to the west of Adrian. A house was hit with dime to quarter size hail, but the worst part of the storm stayed just west of its location.
The strongest wind gust measured was 79mph and occurred at 817pm CDT. There were multiple gusts of 60mph or greater that occurred for nearly ten minutes.
Severe wind gusts occurred for three minutes with the strongest being 65mph at 821pm CDT.
Wind gusts of 58 mph or greater were measured for 5 minutes beginning at 1827CDT.
Hail dented cars as well as some windows were knocked out of a house.
A large tree was blown down in the front yard of a residence. Multiple trees were blown down in the area.
Hail fell around Vega. Most of the hailstones were quarter size but a few were up to golfball size.
The first severe wind gust of 59mph occurred at 2010 CDT, with another 58mph wind gust measured at 2012 CDT and the last 59mph wind gust at 2014 CDT.
Severe wind gusts started at 2017CDT and continued through 2037CDT with peak wind gust of 64mph occurring at 2031CDT.
An outflow boundary moved through the mesonet site located six miles west-southwest of Adrian and produced a wind gust of 58mph.
